scenarios.name: migrate-axum-07-to-08
scenarios.rationale: Both rewrite the routes to `/orders/{id}` and `/assets/{*rest}` and remove `#[async_trait]` in favour of a plain `async fn` in the `FromRequestParts` impl; A also notes that `axum::Server` is gone and that `axum::serve(listener, app)` replaces it, which the rubric allows as optional, while B only says `axum::serve` is unchanged and gives a more complete extractor example.

scenarios.name: bearer-auth-route-layer
scenarios.rationale: Both use an async fn with Request and Next, attach it with route_layer on a protected sub-router merged into the main router, keep /health outside it, and return 401 for bad tokens, so both meet the rubric. B is a complete runnable program using from_fn_with_state and explains why .layer would break 404s. A uses from_fn without state and mentions from_fn_with_state only as an aside, and its token check reads an env var on every request.

scenarios.name: axum-handler-tests-without-db
scenarios.rationale: Both responses satisfy every rubric item: oneshot with Request::builder().uri().body(Body::empty()), a lazy pool, BodyExt collect().await.unwrap().to_bytes(), and asserts of status 200 and body OK. B calls PgPool::connect_lazy directly as the rubric names it and is more concise. A uses PgPoolOptions::new().connect_lazy, which is equivalent, and adds extra notes.
